output_json.patch_notes: Root cause: AbstractResourceHandler.getResource(HttpServletRequest) resolves servletPath/pathInfo into a request path, which ExternalResourceHandler/ClassPathResourceHandler concatenate onto their configured base resource directory via addPaths(), and only then normalize with StringUtils.cleanPath() inside the ExternalResource/ClassPathResource constructors. UriPath.canonical(), called earlier on the raw request path alone, is blind to backslash-delimited '..' and does not know about the base root at all, so it cannot prove the final concatenated path stays contained. Fix: added AbstractResourceHandler.isPathUnderBase(base, candidate), a static helper that cleanPath()-normalizes both the base and the candidate (also normalizing leading-slash presence so it works for both filesystem-style and classpath-relative paths), appends a trailing separator to each, and requires candidate to start with base. Called this check in ExternalResourceHandler.getResource(String) and ClassPathResourceHandler.getResource(String) right after addPaths(baseResource, path) and again after addPaths(resource.getPath(), welcomeFile) in the welcome-file branch of each, returning null (treated as not-found) whenever containment fails. Added 4 new regression tests (2 per handler) exercising both the backslash-based bypass and a plain '/../' request; all pre-existing tests (295 total in the suite) continue to pass unmodified.
output_json.risk_notes: Change is additive (an early-return null guard) and does not alter behavior for any path that stays within the base resource root, so legitimate static-file serving (including welcome-file resolution) is unaffected — confirmed by the full `mvn test` run (295/295 passing, including StaticFilesTest/StaticFilesMemberTest/GenericIntegrationTest which exercise real static-file serving end to end). The POV (.security-pipeline/pov/PathTraversalPovTest.java) now fails with an AssertionError instead of succeeding, confirming the vulnerable behavior is blocked; per instructions its command was not added to regression_commands since the orchestrator runs it separately. The fix relies on StringUtils.cleanPath() for normalization (same utility already trusted downstream by both resource classes), so it inherits that utility's semantics rather than introducing a new parsing path; no filesystem I/O or symlink resolution is required since the check operates purely on the string form of the concatenated path before any File/classloader access occurs.
output_json.summary: Fixed CWE-022 path traversal in spark's static resource handlers. UriPath.canonical() only recognizes '/' as a path separator, so a backslash-based '..' sequence (or any traversal with more '..' segments than consumable preceding segments) passed through unrejected; StringUtils.cleanPath() later normalizes separators and collapses '..' but never rejects leftover '..' that walk above the concatenation root, so the final File/classpath lookup silently escaped the configured base resource directory. Added a shared AbstractResourceHandler.isPathUnderBase(base, candidate) containment check (normalizes both paths via StringUtils.cleanPath, adds leading/trailing '/' boundaries, and requires the candidate to be base or a descendant) and applied it in both ExternalResourceHandler.getResource(String) and ClassPathResourceHandler.getResource(String) immediately after computing the concatenated path and before constructing the ExternalResource/ClassPathResource, as well as after computing the welcome-file re-resolution path in both handlers. This closes all four sink paths in the alert (both handler families, both the direct and welcome-file branches) with one root-cause fix at the trust boundary, since both branches converge on the same addPaths()+cleanPath() pattern.
